messages:
sylvie (infosec): Heads-up: compliance will roll a deny-by-default egress rule in eu-west-1 at 02:00 UTC. This will block some legacy bootstrap hosts and could prevent nodes from fetching ephemeral KMS grants during GPU onboarding.

max (platform): Which hostnames/CIDRs? we should scope a tight exception rather than delaying the rollout.

tere (infra): Quick scan: onboarding calls keystore-eu.internal:443, bootstrap-legacy-2.eu:443 and telemetry 18.130.12.0/24. In staging, blocking them produced `keystore handshake timeout` and warm-pool fill dropped sharply.

olga (sre): Staging numbers: warm-pool 80% -> 38% in ~7m when egress blocked. Cold start p95 increased and we saw more auth-cache hits.

sylvie (infosec): Compliance will allow a 24h scoped exception if you provide exact FQDNs/IPs, a justification, an AZ canary plan, an owner, and bump audit retention for those flows to 180d.

max (platform): I'll open a minimal ACL PR limited to svc:onboard and the three FQDNs, timeboxed 24h. PR: https://git.redwood/fw-regions/pulls/1407. Canary plan: enable per AZ, 4 nodes max, smoke test `curl -sSf https://keystore-eu.internal/health`.

tere (infra): Toggle script: `./ops/onboard --region eu-west-1 --az b --canary on`. Rollback criteria: warm-pool drop >20% or keystore 5xx >1% sustained 5m.

olga (sre): I'll watch metrics and trigger rollback if thresholds hit. audit-bot: please record the PR, approvers, and retention change.

audit-bot: Created ticket AUD-2026-711 "Scoped egress exception eu-west-1 for GPU onboarding" assigned to sylvie (infosec), max (platform).
